name: North Dakota

events.title: Statehood
events.text: North Dakota became the 39th state on November 2, 1889. Congress gave it 1 seat in the House until the next apportionment.

events.title: 1890 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1890 census, North Dakota kept 1 seat in the House. It elected its one member statewide (at-large).

events.title: 1900 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1900 census, North Dakota's House delegation grew from 1 to 2 seats.

events.title: Statewide (general ticket) elections
events.text: In the 58th through 62nd Congresses (1903–1913), North Dakota elected all of its representatives statewide on a general ticket instead of by district.

events.title: 1910 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1910 census, North Dakota's House delegation grew from 2 to 3 seats.

events.title: 1930 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1930 census, North Dakota's House delegation shrank from 3 to 2 seats.

events.title: Statewide (general ticket) elections
events.text: In the 73rd through 87th Congresses (1933–1963), North Dakota elected all of its representatives statewide on a general ticket instead of by district.

events.title: 1940 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1940 census, North Dakota kept 2 seats in the House.

events.title: 1950 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1950 census, North Dakota kept 2 seats in the House.

events.title: 1960 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1960 census, North Dakota kept 2 seats in the House.

events.title: 1970 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1970 census, North Dakota's House delegation shrank from 2 to 1 seat. It elected its one member statewide (at-large).

events.title: 1980 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1980 census, North Dakota kept 1 seat in the House. It elected its one member statewide (at-large).

events.title: 2020 census apportionment

compactnessNote: Polsby-Popper compactness (4π × area ÷ perimeter²) measured on the projected district shapes. It describes shape only: coastlines, rivers and county lines lower it too, so a low score is not evidence of intent. "Irregular" marks the least compact 5% of district shapes in each census era nationally.

c063.text: New map drawn after the 1910 census, which raised North Dakota's seats from 2 to 3. It was first used in the 1912 election.

c073.text: After the 1930 census changed North Dakota's seats from 3 to 2, North Dakota still elected all of its members statewide, so it had no districts to redraw.

c088.text: New map drawn after the 1960 census, which left North Dakota with 2 seats. It was first used in the 1962 election.

c093.text: New map drawn after the 1970 census, which cut North Dakota's seats from 2 to 1. It was first used in the 1972 election.
